None present for the applicant-appellant.

2. Heard learned counsel for the respondents and the Standing Counsel.
3.

The instant restoration application has been filed for restoring the First Appeal No.525 of 2001 (U.P.Awas Evam Vikas Parishad Lko vs Sudhakar Tyagi and others), whereby the appeal has been dismissed for want of prosecution by this Court on 06.03.2018.

entities.text: U.P.Awas Evam Vikas Parishad Lko vs Sudhakar Tyagi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. It is submitted in the restoration application that the order be recalled, the appeal be restored and thereafter, the matter be decided on merits.
5.

Learned counsel for the respondents has opposed the above prayer and has submitted that the appellant has challenged the impugned award and decree dated 08.03.2001 passed by the court of IIIrd Additional District Judge, Moradabad in L.A.R. No.31 of 1988 (Kalyan vs. State), whereby for the land acquired in Village Majhauli, Tehsil and Pargana Moradabad by the U.P. Awas Evam Vikas Parishad in the year 1982, a compensation @ Rs.90 per square meter besides other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act has been awarded to the claimants, which has been enhanced by this Court to Rs.160/- per square meter, since the respondents acquired land was situated in the first belt.

Learned counsel further submitted that even if it is assumed that the respondents land is situated in the third belt, even then, this Court awarded a compensation @
Rs.90 per square meter, which cannot be reduced any further in this appeal, as such, the appellant's prayer for reducing the compensation below Rs.90/- per square meter, cannot be allowed by this Court.
6. Learned counsel submitted that in view of the above facts, the present appeal is meritless and is liable to be dismissed.

7. It is apparent that in the instant case, the respondents' land situated in plot nos.126, 129 and 130 in Village Majhauli, Tehsil and Pargana Moradabad admeasuring 1.21 acre has been acquired by the State Government on behalf of U.P. Awas Evam Vikas Parishad in the year 1982, regarding which the Reference Court has awarded compensation @ Rs.90 per square meter, besides other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, to the respondents.

8. It is also apparent that regarding similarly acquired land, this Court in First Appeal No.896 of 1991 (U.P. Awas Evam Vikas Parishad vs. Jagdish and others) along with 29 other connected U.P.Awas Evam Vikas Parishad Lko. vs Sudhakar Tyagi And Others on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7839349/
2 appeals, vide order dated 29.04.1999 has categorized the awarded land into three belts, regarding the acquired land falling in first belt compensation @ Rs.200/- per square meter, for the acquired land falling in second belt compensation @ Rs.150/- per square meter and for the acquired land falling in third belt compensation @ Rs.100/- per square meter was awarded, which was to be further reduced by the development charges @ 20%, 15% and 10% respectively.

entities.text: U.P. Awas Evam Vikas Parishad vs. Jagdish and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: U.P.Awas Evam Vikas Parishad Lko. vs Sudhakar Tyagi And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also apparent that the above order dated 29.04.1999 of this Court has attained finality because the appeal preferred by the U.P. Awas Evam Vikas Parishad has been dismissed by the Apex Court, vide order dated 01.05.2003.

It is apparent that in terms of the order dated 29.04.1999 of this Court, the compensation for the acquired land in any circumstance cannot be reduced below Rs.90/- per square meter, which has been awarded in this case, by the Reference Court..
9. In view of this, even on merits, this appeal is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed.
10. In view of the above facts, no useful purpose would be served in restoring the instant appeal to its original number.
Accordingly, the restoration application is hereby dismissed.
